Prince Harry exits BetterUp chief role after 5 years on $1 million salary, takes senior adviser post
stories.summary: Prince Harry has stepped down as chief impact officer at BetterUp after five years, moving into a senior adviser role at the US-based mental health and coaching company. The Duke of Sussex reportedly earned $1 million annually during his tenure. The development comes weeks after his return to the UK with Meghan Markle and their children, drawing attention to his professional plans.

stories.title: JD Vance says a lot of infighting, reshuffling going on, people asking if No 2 has what it takes to lead. Then he clarifies he is talking about Ohio State Buckeyes
Ohio residents push data center ban as $5bn Amazon project faces November 10 hearing
stories.summary: Residents in Butler County are rallying against the proposed Amazon data center, voicing worries over possible water shortages, noise pollution, and pollution from backup generators. Local zoning authorities have suggested prohibiting data centers in St. Clair Township, where this project is slated to occur. A crucial public hearing is set to address these issues alongside zoning matters. Recent trends show rising voter favor for restrictions on similar undertakings across Ohio.

stories.title: Diwali is 'Eid of joy', says Kharge; Congress insulting Sanatan culture: BJP
US court rejects malpractice claim over lawyer's missed deadline to correct $100,000 divorce debt error
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, an Arizona appeals court upheld a decision to dismiss a woman's malpractice claim against her ex-attorney. The court concluded she suffered no direct financial loss from the attorney's missed deadline, despite a $200,000 error in the divorce decree regarding familial debt. It was established that the obligation to pay the debt remained unchanged and fully enforceable.

stories.title: 19 runners hospitalized after 'unusual symptoms' at California half-marathon; heat exhaustion might be a reason as Santa Barbara temperatures reached 86 degree Fahrenheit
Michael Jackson's iconic stage glove sells for €113,737 at French auction
Unions dismiss France's 24-euro minimum wage increase
Oregon couple in their 70s win over $8 million after firms foreclose on home they still lived in
stories.summary: An Oregon couple in their 70s have been awarded more than $8 million after a jury found companies liable for unlawfully foreclosing on their home while they were still living in it. The Salem couple had also been denied more than $175,000 left over from the foreclosure sale, which took place in 2022. The jury found that the companies had carried out unlawful trade practices and financially abused the elderly homeowners.

stories.title: Meet Leo Toake, 16, who turned potato peels into weedkiller and restored 15 acres in New Jersey
stories.summary: At just 16 years old, Leo Toake from New Jersey is on a mission to create a revolutionary herbicide sourced from food scraps. Through his nonprofit, Re:Imagine Inc., he's mobilized over 70 volunteers for habitat restoration and invasive species removal. Early trials of Toake's S.A.F.E. clearly show an 82.5% effectiveness against Japanese stilt grass, all while repurposing over 500 pounds of food waste and contributing to a cleaner environment.

stories.title: Kublai Khan’s warship sank in 1281; 745 years later, dice reveal how its crew spent breaks
stories.summary: Archaeologists recently found gaming pieces and dice from a Mongol invasion shipwreck near Takashima Island. These discoveries suggest that sailors engaged in leisure activities during voyages. The ship may measure around 30 metres, potentially the largest of three identified wrecks. Other artefacts discovered nearby include food containers and tools indicative of daily life aboard the ship.

stories.title: Bihar govt bans firecrackers, private boat operations near ghats ahead of Chhath Puja
Delhi Police issues notice to Mamata Banerjee as witness in 2013 protest case
Residents raise $30,000 to bring first grocery store to Alabama neighbourhood in 70 years
stories.summary: After nearly 70 years without a grocery store, Birmingham's Fountain Heights neighbourhood has opened the We All Eat Market. Developed by a local farming cooperative, the $1 million project received $30,000 in grassroots contributions and $150,000 from the city. The market will sell locally grown food, support small farmers and offer discounts to eligible customers.

stories.title: Mona Vale beachfront home fetches record $29 million
stories.summary: A Mona Vale beachfront house recently set a new record by selling for A$29 million in a private sale. The property was previously owned by McDonald's Australia's chief executive and sold for A$7.65 million in 2014. The sale was conducted discreetly without public marketing, ensuring privacy for the owners. The previous record for Mona Vale was A$13.5 million, established in October 2025.

stories.title: 'Anybody believe this was honest?' Trump revives fraud claims after midterm results
Norway’s largest Viking hoard yields rare King Olaf coin not found in country since 1924
stories.summary: A rare coin minted during King Olaf Haraldsson's reign around 1025 has been identified in Norway's Morstad Viking hoard. It is only the second coin of this type found in Norway, the previous one dating back to 1924. The coin also offers clues about the king's use of Christian symbols and its circulation in commercial transactions.

stories.title: Kentucky court keeps father 500 feet from home despite sole ownership claim after wife's death
stories.summary: A Kentucky court has upheld a key decision safeguarding the welfare of two boys by ruling against their father's attempt to rescind protective orders. Although he is the property owner, the court has ordered him to maintain a 500-foot separation from his home. This ruling, following the untimely death of the boys' mother in 2025, emphasizes the priority given to their security over the father's interests.

stories.title: Amateur prospector finds 1.2-kg gold nugget worth A$150,000 in Australia
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, a hobbyist prospector unearthed a significant gold nugget weighing 1,218 grams in New South Wales. With approximately 940 grams of pure gold, its value is estimated between A$150,000 and A$200,000. The Tibooburra area continues to draw gold seekers and tourists, with this nugget serving as a testament to the dedication and perseverance required in the thrilling quest for gold.

stories.title: $180,000 Bitcoin, Pokemon cards feature in North Carolina divorce appeal
stories.summary: A North Carolina appeals court upheld a divorce court's valuation of three Bitcoin at $180,000, Pokemon cards at $1,800 and its unequal division of marital assets. However, it overturned a $15,261.40 attorney’s fee award and an order requiring the husband to pay the entire forensic accountant’s bill, citing missing findings needed to establish the reasonableness of the fees.

stories.title: 'Scrap Rs 500 notes': CM Naidu seeks to phase out big currency to curb corruption
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu advocates for the abolition of Rs 500 and other high-value banknotes to combat corruption and promote a shift to digital transactions, which he believes is vital for economic enhancement. The recent local election results revealed a strong tilt toward the National Democratic Alliance, especially in urban regions, indicating a robust affirmation of democratic ideals and effective governance across Andhra Pradesh.

stories.title: ‘There is only the United States of America’: Erika Kirk slams Abdul El-Sayed’s ‘Arab America’ remark after historic Senate win
Canada has protected more than 81,400 hectares of Ontario taiga forest and peatlands
stories.summary: A significant investment of $64 million is underway to safeguard over 81,400 hectares of taiga forests and peatlands in Ontario. This project focuses on preserving habitats for wildlife, including vulnerable species such as the red-headed woodpecker and the bobolink. It represents Canada's commitment to conserving 30 percent of its lands and waters by 2030 through a collaborative effort involving various organizations, government entities, and private donors.

stories.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault
'There is an old saying': BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari explains her 'firecrackers cure illness' remark, apologises
Idaho reconnected 8 acres of floodplain and built 2,000 feet of side channels
stories.summary: Warm Springs Preserve in Ketchum is currently undergoing significant habitat restoration, aimed at reviving local ecosystems. The initiative includes reconnecting floodplains and building new channels to support aquatic species. An enhanced irrigation system is projected to conserve roughly 50 million gallons of water annually. Furthermore, the project will introduce accessible trails and improved public facilities for the community, marking a commendable step towards better environmental management and habitat preservation.

stories.title: After surveys found only dead oil beetles in 2022 and 2025, volunteers discovered larvae
stories.summary: Exciting news from Pembrokeshire, Wales: conservationists have unearthed short necked oil beetle larvae, a positive sign of the species' reproduction in its sole habitat in the country. Surveys just a year ago had only identified deceased adults. Thanks to the Bumblebee Conservation Trust's diligent monitoring, efforts are in place to safeguard this beetle's ecosystem, emphasizing the vital need to protect its environment for lasting survival.

stories.title: North Carolina court backs review process after father demands $3,000 for children's overseas trips
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a North Carolina Court determined that a parenting coordinator has the authority to dictate travel regulations for divorced parents. This case highlighted conflicts regarding international trips with minors, driven by one parent's financial motivations rather than genuine safety worries. The decision underscores the importance of prioritizing children's welfare in travel arrangements, clarifying parental rights during custody disagreements in North Carolina.

stories.title: Arpita Singh, celebrated artist who painted real women, dies at 89
Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart to Receive First Joint Philanthropy Award
Meet Indian-origin Anjali Sud, the new CEO of SiriusXM, succeeding Jennifer Witz
320 acres around 200-year-old North Carolina iron mine bought to protect five bat species
stories.summary: A former iron mine in North Carolina, which operated from the 1820s to the 1930s, now provides a winter shelter for five bat species, including rare and endangered ones. The Southern Appalachian Highlands Conservancy has purchased 320 acres around the historic mine to protect its underground tunnels, recovering forest and wildlife habitat. The move strengthens earlier conservation efforts to safeguard bats from habitat disturbance and white-nose syndrome, a deadly fungal disease.

stories.title: PM Modi speaks with Zelenskyy, discusses efforts for Russia-Ukraine peace deal
Blue Angels mystery deepens: Officer Daniell Cribb's profile disappears from Navy website after her mentor Scott Laux's dismissal
'I warned you before too': Kejriwal takes swipe at Yogi over SIR, congratulates Akhilesh in advance
'Why spend on R&D?' Rajeev Chandrasekhar mocks China's 'easier way' over Nvidia spy claim
stories.summary: Rajeev Chandrasekhar highlighted the recent honeytrapping allegations against Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang involving China. He criticised China's ethical standards in technology acquisition and alleged espionage practices. China responded by denying these allegations and labeling them as baseless. An independent investigation has been launched by Nvidia's board regarding the claims. Huang has also admitted to personal issues but maintains no national security breaches occurred.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Nvidia boss in Chinese spy scandal; Delhi's AQI turns severe; Iran's hidden oil network in China, and more
Gang posing as Army suppliers dupe Assam firm of Rs 11.5 crore, key accused held in Bengal
BJP's third-term bid, Congress's comeback hopes: What will decide Uttarakhand elections 2027?
Manipur census on hold till April 2027 as high court seeks answers from the Centre
stories.summary: The Manipur high court has ordered the postponement of the Census 2027 until late April 2027. This ruling aims to address significant concerns regarding how recent ethnic violence and subsequent displacements might skew population counts. The court requested the Census Commissioner to review seven representations. Following the authorities' decision, a further four-week delay will apply, allowing anyone unhappy with the outcome to seek legal recourse.

stories.title: Karnataka, Keralam governments launch E20 petrol quality checks amid ethanol blending concerns
stories.summary: The Keralam civil supplies department conducted inspections of petrol pumps in Kochi to examine the ethanol mix in E20 petrol. Officials took six samples, forwarding two for lab tests in Kakinada. Rising concerns over high ethanol blending have been highlighted by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad. However, the union ministry of petroleum claims all samples adhere to quality norms, disputing allegations of excessive mixing.

stories.title: India, Lebanon hold first Foreign Office consultations; discuss trade, investment, digital cooperation
stories.summary: India and Lebanon embarked on their first-ever Foreign Office Consultations in New Delhi, aiming to strengthen their bilateral relationship. Important topics of discussion included cooperation in political-security, economic, and socio-cultural arenas. Ambassador Sripriya Ranganathan's visit to Lebanon set the stage for deeper ties, as key areas like trade, investment, digital infrastructure, and pharmaceuticals were reviewed, along with pressing regional and international matters.

stories.title: 'He called us Naxals': Rahul Gandhi hits back at PM Modi, renews debate challenge
'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark
stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge stirred controversy by referring to Diwali as 'khushiyon ka Eid'. BJP officials accused the Congress of misrepresenting Diwali, asserting each festival has its unique identity. Pawan Khera of Congress defended Kharge's statement, emphasizing the meaning of 'Eid' as 'festival.' The BJP responded by questioning the appropriateness of comparing Diwali with Eid, which they deemed disrespectful. This disagreement highlights ongoing political tensions regarding religious and cultural identities.

stories.title: Delhi pollution sparks row: BJP alleges 'conspiracy'; AAP and Congress question AQI data
Jaishankar extends national day greetings to Cambodia, hails strong civilisational ties
stories.summary: S Jaishankar conveyed warm National Day wishes to Cambodia, celebrating the deep-rooted civilizational connections between the two countries. He praised the successful conclusion of the recent Cambodia-India Bilateral Army Exercise, CINBAX-II, which focused on collaborative training to bolster operational synergy among their armed forces. The exercise allowed both teams to display their professionalism and exchange valuable operational insights, further solidifying the defense partnership between India and Cambodia.

stories.title: Wisconsin family manages 500-acre forest for wildlife and timber; shortlisted for state conservation award
stories.summary: Jesse and Kylie Sebero are managing over 500 acres of forest in Marinette County, Wisconsin. They focus on timber production while ensuring ecological balance and wildlife conservation. The couple also opens their land for educational tours, helping others learn about forest management. They have been nominated for the 2026 Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award for their significant contributions. The award will be announced during an upcoming meeting on November 12.

stories.title: South Carolina woman protects 146-acre family land after promise to mother
stories.summary: Alice Smith has placed her family's 146-acre property in South Carolina under a conservation easement, fulfilling a promise to her mother. Her grandparents bought the land in the 1940s. Along with another family, she has permanently restricted development on more than 250 acres through Upstate Forever.

stories.title: South Carolina father arrested after leaving 6-year-old alone for Pokemon cards
Princess Margaret's wedding gift: Mustique villa now rents for $50,000 a week
'True colours exposed': BJP's Giriraj Singh tears into Kharge over Diwali 'khushiyon ka Eid' remark
‘We’re losing a hell of a lot’: Cessna carrying 5 men vanished over Australia in 1981; 45 years later, no trace found
stories.summary: In August of 1981, a Cessna aircraft disappeared in Australia's Barrington Tops, carrying five men. Despite numerous searches and thorough investigations, both the plane and its passengers were never discovered. Reports indicated that severe turbulence and ice accumulation likely played a role in the incident. The mystery remains captivating for amateur sleuths and volunteers, while the families of the missing continue their quest for answers about their loved ones' fate.

stories.title: Doctors are using bacteria-killing viruses against superbugs that drugs cannot beat
stories.summary: Amidst the rising concern over antibiotic resistance, doctors are turning to phage therapy, a novel approach that employs viruses to target and eliminate dangerous bacteria. A recent Belgian study found that over 77% of patients showed significant clinical improvement. To enhance the application of personalized bacteriophage treatments, new international guidelines have been introduced, though researchers underline the importance of further studies to comprehend the therapy's potential fully.

stories.title: Ohio man keeps premarital home after divorce; wife ordered to pay $20,000 in legal fees
stories.summary: In a pivotal divorce ruling in Ohio, the court upheld the husband's ownership of his pre-marital property, rejecting the wife's assertions about marital contributions from their joint bank account. The trial court mandated that she pay $20,000 towards his legal expenses, reflecting on her actions throughout the proceedings. The husband's rental income was deemed adequate to maintain mortgage obligations, highlighting the relevance of asset tracking in such cases.

stories.title: Katy Perry and Russell Brand’s former estate rents for $275,000 monthly
High-Rise Fire Kills 14: Blaze rips through Taiyuan tower; authorities probe cause amid safety drive
stories.summary: On Sunday afternoon, a devastating fire erupted in a downtown high-rise building in Taiyuan, China. Firefighters responded swiftly, bringing the flames under control about two hours later, by 7 pm local time. The rescue efforts lasted until 8:30 pm, leading to the evacuation and hospitalization of 38 individuals. The unfortunate event initially reported five deaths, which later rose to 14 confirmed fatalities.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'
stories.summary: Sheikh Hasina has applied for a new passport and national identity card, indicating her intent to return and address the legal matters awaiting her in Bangladesh. Despite a prior ban, her Awami League party continues to enjoy robust support. Her return is likely to heighten the existing political unrest and may further complicate India-Bangladesh relations, as discussions on her extradition unfold.

stories.title: Chancellor Merz backs Ilse Aigner as Germany's first female President
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has endorsed Ilse Aigner for the upcoming presidential election in Germany. Aigner, if elected, would be the first woman to hold this position. Supported by the Christian Democratic Union and the Christian Social Union, she has backing from various political parties. She could succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose presidency ends on March 18. Aigner has previous government experience and a strong political network in Germany.

stories.title: ‘Task Force Iron Gate in full force' to choke Iran's trade route, says Trump
stories.summary: Task Force Iron Gate is a new US initiative aimed at disrupting Iran's overland supply routes and preventing advanced weapons movement. It involves around 20 personnel coordinating with various US agencies from Tampa, Florida. The task force complements an existing naval blockade that has already hindered Iran's oil exports significantly. Humanitarian aid will remain exempt from these restrictions despite the new measures.

stories.title: 'Immigration policy too tough': 5 key takeaways from Trump's 60 minutes interview
stories.summary: Donald Trump admitted in a recent interview that the Iran war and deportation policies affected Republican midterm results. He acknowledged that while strong border security was supported, harsh deportation measures raised concerns among voters. Trump expressed a willingness to negotiate with Democrats on immigration reform, particularly for long-term residents. He maintained that Iran was prevented from obtaining nuclear weapons during his presidency, asserting military involvement in the region.

stories.title: 'Dimagi Naxal' remark a brazen assault: Congress
Texas family donates historic cave to protect four million mother bats and pups
Peat from ancient forests off Mozambique dates back up to about 5,000 years
stories.summary: Submerged ancient peat forests off Mozambique's coast have transformed into vibrant marine ecosystems, offering vital habitats for diverse marine life. As rising sea levels allowed these forests to sink, they have now integrated with coral reefs, enhancing local biodiversity. The carbon-rich legacy of these underwater realms also holds significant implications for climate strategies, highlighting the necessity of including peat reefs in conservation initiatives.

stories.title: South Carolina permanently protected more than 62,000 acres of working forest
stories.summary: South Carolina has successfully protected over 62,000 acres of forestland with the Pee Dee Basin Initiative. This initiative represents a significant collaboration among various government and private organizations, totaling an investment of $70 million. The protected areas will support sustainable timber production while preventing incompatible development that undermines ecological integrity. In addition, this initiative will enhance local wildlife habitats and strengthen natural flood defenses for surrounding communities.

stories.title: Reds gone, but 'dimagi Naxals' still instigating people: PM Modi
Baby pufferfish inherit a nearly non-toxic chemical from their mothers
stories.summary: In a fascinating discovery, researchers have found that mother pufferfish provide their larvae with a nearly non-toxic chemical that effectively helps them escape predators. This chemical deters potential threats by making them unpalatable, thus improving the young fish's chances of survival. Additionally, this same chemical intriguingly attracts other pufferfish, revealing a unique dual role that aids in their survival strategies during vulnerable stages.

stories.title: Stanford scientists have built a fingernail-sized chip that turns jumbled light into clean beams
stories.summary: Stanford University researchers have developed a groundbreaking chip that effectively segregates mixed light into its individual components. This novel technology facilitates the analysis of coherence modes of light that were once challenging to identify. Utilizing advanced photonic techniques, the chip can enhance applications in fields like imaging and astronomy, potentially transforming our understanding of microscopic particles and faraway celestial phenomena.

stories.title: Meet 14-year-old Jacob who grows 7,000 tomato plants for his business
High Court dismisses farm claims by Richard Scott’s son and stepmother
16-year-old builds free wildfire warning checker, teaches California seniors to use it after brush fire
stories.summary: Vedant Thakker created the Red Flag Check application to evaluate wildfire risks utilizing data from the National Weather Service. This innovative tool classifies residential locations under red flag warnings into four specific risk categories, empowering local residents. It is specially designed for older adults who may face increased vulnerability during wildfires.

stories.title: Firehouse Townhouse Sells: Former Manhattan station fetches $19m; includes underground jazz club
stories.summary: A historic fire station in Manhattan has been transformed into a luxury townhouse and sold for $19 million. It originally served the community as a firehouse for over a century before being decommissioned. The property underwent extensive renovations, highlighting its unique features such as an underground jazz club. Notably, the townhouse retains elements of its industrial past while incorporating modern living spaces.

stories.title: Historic Brooklyn mansion returns to market for $20.99M
stories.summary: Once a forgotten gem, a historic mansion in Brooklyn Heights from 1852 has been meticulously transformed and is now available for $14.99 million. The adjacent carriage house can be purchased separately for $6 million. After a decade-long renovation focused on preserving its original beauty while integrating luxury amenities, this estate invites potential buyers to explore various living arrangements, from family homes to vibrant workspaces.

stories.title: Billionaire couple's $50 million gift leads to new UC Davis research centre
Built for $45,000 in 1965, this Pasadena glass house now seeks $3.25 million
Taraji P. Henson's foundation backs $30 million wellness hub in Maryland
Brazil expands Pantanal reserves by 257,531 acres to protect jaguar habitats
Cold War Greenland base was ice-free 416,000 years ago, summers 4.7°C warmer
How two Wisconsin students built a volunteer network to fight hunger
stories.summary: In Middleton, Wisconsin, Noah Duckett and Wyatt Ehrhardt launched a food drive aimed at tackling food insecurity. This initiative blossomed into Meals Matter, a national non-profit featuring over 35 student-led chapters. With more than $550,000 raised and countless young volunteers participating nationwide, both founders were honored with The Diana Award, showcasing how youth can lead transformative social change.

stories.title: Rotten Roots: family turns yard into walk-through Halloween haunt; visitors trigger effects
stories.summary: In Pennsylvania, a family has dedicated five years to crafting an enchanting Halloween experience known as Rotten Roots. This immersive yard display combines a thrilling storyline of witches and alien invaders with interactive decorations, enhanced through a special app. As they continue to expand their attraction with new characters and mechanics, the family fosters deeper bonds within the local Halloween enthusiast community.

stories.title: 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb reveals 1,000 cannabis seeds and evidence of ritual intoxication
stories.summary: A groundbreaking archaeological find at Tunnug 1 in southern Siberia unveiled cannabis seeds within a prince's tomb, dating back 2,800 years. This tomb is tied to intricate funerary rites, including horse sacrifices. Notably, preserved human hair revealed traces of cannabis, hinting at its psychoactive use, which underscores cannabis's significant role in ancient burial customs. Researchers plan to conduct further DNA analysis to deepen the understanding of its historical relevance.

stories.title: New Mexico artist gives a 1953 Chevy Bel Air a second life as a jackrabbit
stories.summary: Robert Wilson crafted an impressive sculpture of a jackrabbit from salvaged components of a 1953 Chevrolet Bel Air. Titled Run, this artwork symbolizes the rich heritage of Route 66 through its creative design. Towering at over 10 feet, it is richly detailed to reflect its automotive origins. Situated in Babe Ruth Park, Gallup, this piece celebrates the 100th anniversary of the legendary highway, inviting visitors to appreciate its artistry.

stories.title: Georgia couple's $40,000 basement renovation sparks divorce property dispute
444-million-year-old fossil preserves muscles but loses head and legs
Josh Duhamel and Bobcat donate utility vehicle to Los Angeles firefighters
Omaha apartment owner's civil rights lawsuit over 2018 closure rejected by appeals court
stories.summary: A federal appeals court confirmed the dismissal of civil rights claims by AB Realty against Omaha officials. The lawsuit arose after the city shut down a building due to code violations in 2018. Despite the claims alleging Fourth, Fifth, and Fourteenth Amendment violations, the court found insufficient evidence to support them. The ruling highlighted that the city had acted according to legal standards during the inspections.

stories.title: Birds flap their wings while landing even though it costs energy, new model explains why
stories.summary: Research shows that birds flap their wings while landing to enhance control and deceleration. The energy expended during flapping has tangible benefits for a safe landing. Mathematical modeling indicates that a zero-speed landing without flapping is impractical for most birds. Birds of prey may also swoop to manage touchdown speed and avoid stalling before landing.

stories.title: Ferrero to acquire Purely Elizabeth, the wellness food brand founded by Elizabeth Stein
Azores Glider Emergency Landing: Fuel leak turns A330 into 65-nautical-mile glider; all 306 survive
stories.summary: In August 2001, an Air Transat flight traveling from Canada to Portugal experienced a dramatic failure, losing both engines mid-flight. The skilled pilots successfully glided for 19 minutes before executing an emergency landing at Lajes Air Base in the Azores. Remarkably, all 306 on board survived despite injuries from the hard landing.

stories.title: Louisiana court backs homeowner's right to block neighbours from private road beyond 1,000 feet
stories.summary: Mona Matherne spent over a decade contesting neighbors' use of a private road beside her country home. In November 2026, state appeals judges upheld her property rights and confirmed previous court orders. Matherne successfully argued against her neighbors, who claimed the road was public. The court ruled that only the first 1,000 feet was public, protecting Matherne's privacy.

stories.title: Ohio man keeps premarital home as court upholds $20,000 legal-fee award against ex-wife
stories.summary: The Ohio Court of Appeals has upheld that a husband retains ownership of his pre-marriage house, resisting claims from his ex-wife. The judges clarified that the use of rental income for payments did not affect the house's classification as separate property. Moreover, the court ordered his ex-spouse to cover $20,000 in legal fees, highlighting the tensions caused by her legal maneuvers throughout their prolonged dispute.

stories.title: Delhi records 'very poor' air quality on Diwali, 19 monitoring stations report severe AQI
Ohio homeowner ordered to pay contractor $45,806 despite cosmetic defects in basement walls
stories.summary: An Ohio homeowner was ordered to pay a contractor $45,806 for a concrete foundation with cosmetic flaws. The court found that structural integrity was maintained, despite visible surface defects. The homeowner had initially refused payment, claiming that the imperfections reduced property value. The appeals court upheld the lower court decision, emphasizing the importance of structural safety over cosmetic issues.

stories.title: Trump says US took ‘giant step back in history’ after Democrats’ midterm victory
PM Modi visits LK Advani on his birthday as veteran BJP leader enters 100th year
‘Matter of personal faith’: Congress on Akhilesh Yadav’s proposed Ram Temple visit
'Why funding only for temples?' Congress's Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Bengal's Rs 1,000-crore plan
North Dakota woman loses $110,000 home improvement claim after breakup with partner
stories.summary: After her relationship concluded, Mary Roth pursued the return of over $110,000 she invested in home enhancements. However, the North Dakota Supreme Court determined that she could not secure restitution through an unjust enrichment claim. The ruling underscored that Roth needed to demonstrate an actual financial benefit to the property owner, something her receipts failed to do when it came to increasing the property's market value.

stories.title: Rare Altdorfer landscape hidden for 70 years after 1957 acquisition could fetch £5 million
stories.summary: An undiscovered masterpiece by Albrecht Altdorfer, the renowned German Renaissance painter, is set to hit the auction block at Sotheby's this December. This exquisite work, featuring a stunning forest scene crowned by a rainbow, has been held privately since 1957. With Altdorfer's oil landscapes being incredibly scarce, this auction represents a rare chance for collectors, the first of its kind since 1980, including viewings in New York and London beforehand.

stories.title: Egypt train collision: Several injured as train derails after hitting another train
Queen Elizabeth II’s final days at Balmoral Castle: Inside her 53,000-acre Scottish sanctuary
stories.summary: Queen Elizabeth II spent her final days at Balmoral Castle, her beloved Scottish retreat spanning 53,000 acres. The royal estate held decades of cherished family memories, offering her peace and comfort amid nature. From royal summer holidays to her final moments, discover why Balmoral remained one of the Queen’s most treasured places throughout her life.

stories.title: A €20 flea-market lamp sells for €251,000 after hidden signature is discovered
West Virginia court overturns $31,054 home value payout but protects wife's mortgage share
stories.summary: The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals has overturned a previous decision regarding a premarital home. The court ruled that the husband is not liable for the home's market value increase during marriage. This ruling clarifies how separate property and marital contributions are treated in divorce cases. However, the former wife is entitled to financial interest from mortgage principal payments made during the marriage.

stories.title: Far-right wingnuts storm Diwali fest in Seattle after lights go out on MAGA
‘Not a political book, but a personal one’: Sonia Gandhi ahead of memoir release
North Dakota court bars unmarried couples from jointly adopting children, despite parental consent
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, North Dakota’s Supreme Court ruled that unmarried couples are barred from adopting a child together, as dictated by existing state law. This case involved a grandmother and her partner who intended to adopt her grandchild, with agreement from both biological parents. The court clarified that only legislative changes can alter adoption laws, while allowing individual adoption requests from either of the parties involved.

stories.title: Florida appeals court orders fresh review after wife loses alimony and all parenting time following pay cut
stories.summary: In an emerging divorce case from Florida, the Fourth District Court has called for a deeper examination of the rulings made by the Broward County trial court involving Rebecca Zalkin and Jeffrey Zalkin. The initial decision denied alimony and granted sole parental responsibility to the husband without sufficient reasoning. The appellate court highlighted the necessity for validated income data and adherence to legal protocol.

stories.title: 'Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha' actress Shin Min-a quietly donated over $2.7 million in 15 years to help burn victims, underprivileged children and vulnerable families
stories.summary: Since 2009, South Korean actress Shin Min-a has made a remarkable impact through her charitable donations, amounting to more than 3.7 billion won for various causes. Focusing on aiding burn victims, disadvantaged youth, and disaster-affected areas, her annual contributions of 100 million won reported by the Hallym Burn Foundation could total 1.1 billion won by 2026.

stories.title: Australia reverses military land sale plans after protests, saving four historic sites
stories.summary: The Australian government has opted to retain four significant historical military sites in public hands, responding to widespread public dissent against their potential sale. Notably, Victoria Barracks in Sydney and other sites in Victoria will remain untouched. The government aims to find new public purposes for these locations while preserving their heritage, and part of the broader reforms includes returning certain military lands to Indigenous communities.

stories.title: Evening Newswrap: PM Modi warns of 'Dimagi Naxals', Mamata joins Abhishek Banerjee's protest & more
At least 21 dead after migrant boat sinks off Senegal's northwestern coast
Chicago’s World’s Fair featured a two-speed moving sidewalk carrying visitors to the Peristyle

Although video evidence did not support her account of the visit, three earlier incidents of physical violence provided grounds for the order.

stories.title: Meet Pooja Verma, who built bird boxes that photograph nesting birds every three minutes
stories.summary: California student Pooja Verma has won first place in the 36th ‘A Voice for Animals’ contest for developing solar-powered bird boxes with cameras that photograph nesting birds every three minutes. Her nonprofit, Eco Innovate, has distributed the boxes to 10 schools and plans to expand the project across California and the US.

stories.title: High drama in Kolkata: Mamata Banerjee joins TMC workers in protest against attack on Abhishek's home
Florida governor Ron DeSantis denies plans for 2028 presidential run, calls report ‘fabricated’
'Remove your Italian lenses': BJP slams Sonia Gandhi for remarks on country's progress
'A soulful rendition’: Rajnath Singh shares video of IAF warriors' patriotic melody
stories.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh shared a video showcasing Indian Air Force personnel singing a patriotic song. He praised their musical talent, stating it reflects their dedication to serving the country. Singh emphasized the importance of remaining vigilant against evolving national security threats and misinformation. He addressed air warriors at Bagdogra Air Force Station, highlighting the need for operational readiness in modern warfare.

stories.title: Diwali gift for UP govt employees: DA raised to 63%, revised allowance to be paid with November salary
Earth has a new mini-moon: Tiny asteroid 2026 QQ8 was captured in April, spotted in August and will leave by early 2027
stories.summary: A minor asteroid, known as 2026 QQ8, found its way into Earth's gravity in April 2026. Observed for the first time in August, astronomers identified it as a natural celestial body. This mini-moon will remain within our orbit for approximately eight to nine months before departing. Its nearest approach is calculated to be 568,000 kilometers away, carrying no threat of impact as it joins the transient mini-moon collection around Earth.

stories.title: Malaysia's king warns against challenging Najib Razak's house-arrest pardon after $12 million fine paid
stories.summary: Sultan Ibrahim of Malaysia has cautioned against any attempts to contest the conditional pardon granted to Najib Razak for house arrest. The process of Najib's transfer from prison has stalled as authorities seek legal clarification on the pardon’s implications. The attorney-general emphasized that the goal is merely to address legal uncertainties, not to challenge the King's directive.

stories.title: ‘My family, I face threat’: Italy minister says his private data leaked on dark web
stories.summary: Antonio Tajani, Italy's foreign minister, revealed that his personal information is being circulated by cybercriminals on the dark web. This alarming situation has led to threats against him and his family. Tajani indicated these criminals are seeking more personal details. However, he remains resolute in enhancing security collaboration and reaffirmed Italy's steadfast support for Ukraine despite these ongoing threats.

stories.title: 'ED is not a super cop': Karnataka HC quashes ECIR against Congress MLA, others
TikTok accused of becoming a gateway to the online sex industry for young girls
stories.summary: TikTok faces accusations of inadvertently promoting an online sex industry targeting young women and girls. Recent research highlights how popular OnlyFans creators use subtle cues in TikTok videos. These performers appear to endorse financial independence through selling adult content while circumventing platform restrictions. Additionally, TikTok's algorithm contributes to the circulation of these videos among teenagers. Advocates call for stricter regulations to protect minors from adult content influences across social media.

stories.title: Utah millionaire father of seven built a 300-acre doomsday compound stocked with food, weapons and supplies to shelter 200 people if civilisation collapses
stories.summary: Jayson Orvis has created a 300-acre doomsday sanctuary in the heart of Utah, designed to accommodate 200 people during catastrophic circumstances. This unique compound showcases greenhouses and a flourishing food forest, underpinning his vision of cooperative survival. While Orvis maintains a level of skepticism about imminent apocalypse risks, he acknowledges the importance of community over solitude in potential crises.

stories.title: Texas court upholds refinery's gross negligence in worker's death, cuts award by $125,000
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court upheld a refinery company's gross negligence in a worker's asbestos-related death but reduced his family's damages award from $325,000 to $200,000. It also revived negligence claims that had earlier been dismissed, allowing the family to pursue them in further proceedings.

stories.title: Cancer in India: Screening exists, but why are patients still diagnosed late
PG doctors quit premier medical institutes
stories.summary: RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER; numbers decline at Delhi AIIMS and JIPMER, but several institutes lack consolidated records on counselling and workplace stress

stories.title: Massive anti-drug drive: 458 acres of illicit cannabis eradicated in Arunachal Pradesh
BJP attacks Rahul over 'out of context' Amit Shah video amid SIR row
Sharad Pawar discharged from hospital, doctor shares health update
Wedding ring lost on Dutch farm during WWII, found 83 years later
stories.summary: A Dutch man who lost his wedding ring while threshing grain in 1942 or 1943 has had it returned to his family 83 years later. A metal detector user found it buried 20 centimetres underground in Odiliapeel and personally returned it to the owner's son, Bert Nabuurs, refusing a reward. The ring's engraved wedding date confirmed its identity.

stories.title: ‘Relief to breathe Kerala’s clean air’: Shashi Tharoor takes swipe at Delhi govt over pollution crisis
'Democratic rights were curtailed but constitutionally': Sonia Gandhi reflects on Emergency
Als Nursing Hospital Opens: 14-year ALS drive builds specialised facility; 350,000 donors fund care
stories.summary: In March 2025, the Seungil Hope Nursing Hospital in Yongin welcomed its first ALS patients, marking a 14-year journey led by dedicated advocates Park Seung-il and Sean. This landmark facility, developed with the generosity of over 350,000 donors and government backing, aims to provide advanced care tailored to the unique needs of those with ALS, emphasizing a community's unwavering commitment to enhancing the lives of affected individuals.

stories.title: Two men charged over shooting at Kapil Sharma's restaurant in Canada
‘E20 turned into 420’: Rahul Gandhi alleges petrol samples from Karnataka exceed 20% ethanol limit
Republicans spent more, Democrats won more: Inside the costliest US midterm battle
stories.summary: In the 2026 US midterm elections, Democrats made notable gains among Latino voters, following a period of prior support for Republicans. Increased spending by GOP candidates did not secure the anticipated wins, resulting in losses in key districts. High turnout from Latino constituents significantly impacted voting dynamics nationwide, with many responding negatively to proposed data centre projects.

stories.title: 'No permanent solution': Congress slams Delhi govt as pollution levels remain severe
'Who has time to kill him?' BJP-TMC spar after attack on Abhishek Banerjee's house
France deploys 70,000 security personnel ahead of fresh nationwide protests
stories.summary: French trade unions and student groups are organizing a day of protests against rising living costs. The Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris, despite an official ban on gatherings. Nationwide demonstrations have been ongoing for weeks, with participants demanding wage increases and better conditions for youth. On Monday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will meet with union representatives to discuss these issues.

stories.title: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
stories.summary: The United States has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program. This reward aims to gather details about facilities, equipment, and personnel involved with the program. Diplomatic efforts are ongoing to resolve tensions and prevent further conflict. Iran has expressed the desire for negotiations but requires certain conditions to be met.

stories.title: US-China trade talks to continue as Washington presses Beijing to honour Busan deal
stories.summary: China and the US are engaged in ongoing dialogues to foster stable trade relations, with emphasis on prior commitments. US officials expressed concern regarding China's adherence to agreements related to rare earth materials and agricultural products. The latest discussions revealed the US's stance that China falls short in fulfilling its responsibilities under the Busan agreement. Moreover, China dismissed accusations of inadequate rare earth supplies and agricultural purchasing.

stories.title: SC to NewsClick: Reply to ED plea against HC order quashing ECIR
'Voices in head said to kill Trump': Man with firearms and ammunition arrested near White House
stories.summary: The Secret Service took Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos into custody after he exhibited alarming conduct in his vehicle. When confronted by officers, he insisted that he heard voices commanding him to execute President Trump. A subsequent search of his stolen car revealed three guns and additional ammunition. A Venezuelan national without legal status since March 2024, Chrinos now underscores the persistent dangers faced by the president.

stories.title: ED tracking $1m transfer to 'meddle in domestic affairs'
CBI files case against Biyanis, Future Retail in Rs 904 cr fraud
Creamy layer verdict only for those who challenged government decision, says SC
SC settles 60-yr Bhakra & Beas dispute between Punjab, Haryana and HP
Ankit Baliyan murder case: Take us to UP in shackles, bulletproof jackets, plead undertrials
Texas appeals court upholds $619K judgment against beverage company co-owner
'Dallas' star Victoria Principal, 76, now rescues animals on her ranch; shares miniature horse Halo's recovery
stories.summary: Former actress Victoria Principal has found her true calling in animal rehabilitation, dedicating her life to caring for rescued creatures at her ranch. One notable resident is Halo, a miniature horse currently healing with her support. Principal passionately advocates for the role of love and patience in nurturing these animals back to health, marking a significant departure from her Hollywood days as she embraces her new purpose.

stories.title: SC: Awareness alone can curb pollution; people violate restrictions ‘with vengeance’
'Jackass' star Steve-O turns 44-acre Tennessee ranch into a home for rescued animals
stories.summary: Steve-O, the famous Jackass star, has dedicated himself to animal welfare by establishing The Radical Ranch, a sanctuary for rescued animals situated near Nashville. Since its inception as a nonprofit in 2024, the ranch has provided a home for nine animals, including goats and pigs. Steve-O envisions expanding the sanctuary to include cows and chickens while fostering empathy towards all creatures.

stories.title: PM cites Para Games success to motivate athletes for Olympics 2028
Manipur rebel arrested from Delhi hotel
In 2017, Gaten Matarazzo helped form a charity; nine years later, its partners issued 37 care tips
stories.summary: Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD) affects bone and dental development in patients and requires specialized care. A recent study established 37 expert recommendations for diagnosing and managing this rare condition effectively. These guidelines emphasize the importance of coordinated care among various specialists and regular monitoring. Gaten Matarazzo, who has CCD, advocates for better recognition and treatment of the disorder. CCD Smiles organization aims to support patients through awareness and research initiatives.

stories.title: Post on CJI: SC's contempt notice to Keralam Cong office-bearers
With working strength of just 2, Sikkim HC unable to hear intra-court appeals
California condo parking dispute ends after decade; court rejects $292,544 legal fee claim
stories.summary: In a contentious parking dispute in Orange County, condominium owners WCST Enterprises and Berit Ling faced off in court. Ultimately, the court ruled in favor of WCST, affirming its claim to garage space 38G-a. However, despite the legal victory, WCST could not reclaim its substantial legal fees of $292,544, as these claims did not meet California statutes for fee recovery.

stories.title: 125-year-old Idaho ranch gets permanent protection
stories.summary: A conservation easement has been established on the Flying A Ranch in Idaho to protect the land. This easement allows the Atchley family to continue their farming operations while preventing future development. The agreement also supports a crucial wildlife migration corridor for mule deer and various other species. Previous efforts to protect the ranch were led by Clen Atchley, who passed away in 2024.

stories.title: Court allows more evidence in Sonia Gandhi voter list case
HC judge vacancies at decade-low 26%, but pendency keeps piling up
NMC adds 9,783 PG medical seats, takes total to 68,305
New research rules out the theory of Stonehenge Altar Stone's Northeast Scottish Origin
stories.summary: Researchers continue to explore the origins of the Altar Stone at Stonehenge, which weighs approximately six tonnes. Recent studies suggested a possible origin from northeast Scotland, but findings have complicated this theory. A new international team's research found no matching source from the Scottish locations they examined, narrowing possibilities down. Previous assumptions about the Altar Stone's Welsh origins have been challenged by new geological insights.

stories.title: Brisbane Library House Auction: former private library cleared for sale; rebuild interest grows
stories.summary: After years of neglect, a three-bedroom home in Wynnum, Brisbane, has undergone a remarkable transformation. This property, once filled with a vast collection of books and memorabilia, required extensive teamwork to clear out its contents and evict wildlife. Now, it's being showcased as an exciting renovation or rebuilding opportunity in a sought-after neighborhood, with an auction date set for November 14, 2026, drawing potential buyers eager to invest.

stories.title: CBSE Class X & XII board exams to start from Feb 16
More than 30% ethanol in E20, says Karnataka minister
Ousted Videocon promoter Dhoot declared bankrupt over dues worth Rs 12,668cr
One more chance for excluded voters in Delhi, 6 other states
Louisiana woman fights uncle over mother's estate for 13 years; court revives part of lawsuit
stories.summary: A Louisiana woman accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of her late mother's estate to himself and businesses linked to him. More than 23 years after her mother's death, an appeals court revived her claims concerning his handling of the estate but upheld the dismissal of other claims. It also cancelled a $10,000 damages award and ordered further proceedings.

stories.title: For more than 60 years, visitors walked through a cave in Spain; now 280 motifs identified
stories.summary: A remarkable archaeological find at Cova de la Font Major has revealed 280 Palaeolithic engravings, showcasing diverse motifs of animals and geometric shapes. This challenges the previously held notion that cave art was scarce in northeastern Iberia, where only two pieces were known. These engravings suggest the existence of unique artistic traditions independent of the famous Franco-Cantabrian region, offering new insights into the cultural practices of Ice Age Europe.

stories.title: North Carolina student wins top award for free tool mapping wildlife roadkill hotspots
stories.summary: Aaryan Ghorpade, a North Carolina student, has triumphed in a national competition with EcoRoute, a project that tracks wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots across the U.S. This innovative online tool gathers collision data and produces heat maps to assist transportation agencies in improving road safety. EcoRoute also encourages community involvement, allowing users to report wildlife sightings. Ghorpade envisions further enhancements and plans to partner with wildlife conservation organizations in his state.

stories.title: Indian family seeks help to bring back man's body after he dies from burn injuries in New Zealand on birthday
Stephen King's Maine mansion becomes a literary archive, with $2,500 writers' retreats next door
stories.summary: Stephen King and Tabitha have innovatively turned their Bangor residence into a unique archive and retreat for writers. This initiative offers aid and an inspiring atmosphere, allowing selected authors to immerse themselves in their work. The nearby Brown Mansion will serve as an additional haven, benefitting a variety of literary talents, including educators and Maine local writers.

stories.title: Streamer Feud Over Halloween: Banks slams Plaqueboymax’s ‘whiteface’ stream; questions career slide
stories.summary: Plaqueboymax’s Halloween livestream led to disagreements with Adin Ross and FaZe Banks. Adin suggested a blackface stream after seeing Max’s crew dressed as stereotypical white men. Max questioned Adin’s respect for Black culture, while Banks said Max’s costume showed disrespect towards white people. Banks also criticised Max’s content, career direction and Super Bowl halftime show ambitions, and invoked Kai Cenat.

stories.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle back to US after shameful exit from Greece; moved in with ex-husband with a hit list: Report
What led to Susie Wiles' firing within 3 days of Trump's midterm loss? 'Ice maiden' was Trump's longest serving chief of staff
stories.summary: Susie Wiles fired: Within three days of midterm rout, President Donald Trump elevated Stephen Miller to the post of Chief of Staff replacing Susie Wiles, who served the longest on the post. The decision was not out of the blue as there were speculations which the president at that time dismissed.

stories.title: Who is Navneet Alag? Meet husband of newly elected Indian-American congresswoman Pia Dandiya
How Abdullahs managed the rebellion: Farooq calls MLAs’ demands genuine, Omar offers to resign
Meryl Streep backs women's history education as two teachers earn award for AP course campaign
stories.summary: Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams from Sacred Heart Preparatory have pioneered an Advanced Placement course focused on women's history, garnering endorsement from 100 esteemed universities and colleges. This initiative underscores the vital role women have played throughout history. An eminent gala in Chicago on November 6, 2026, will unveil the inaugural Meryl Streep Educator Award, with proceeds dedicated to bolstering educational resources for women's history.

stories.title: Will you comply with Japanese laws? Japan plans new question for foreign visitors on entry form
London councillors reject Berkeley Homes plan after affordable housing offer falls from 40% to 12%
stories.summary: Southwark Council's planning committee voted unanimously against Berkeley Homes' revised plans for the Bermondsey Place development. The housebuilder proposed reducing affordable housing from 40 percent to just 12 percent, causing strong local opposition. Council members expressed concerns about the long timeline for home completion and questioned the developer's financial figures. Berkeley Homes highlighted rising costs and council fees as reasons for the reduced affordable housing offer.

stories.title: Court upholds sale of divorced Arkansas woman's property share after her bankruptcy filing.
stories.summary: In a landmark ruling, a federal appeals court upheld the sale of a divorced woman's stake in property located in Arkansas. The decision favored her bankruptcy trustee, overcoming objections posed by her ex-husband. He contended that the buyer's good faith was not adequately proven in prior hearings but failed to voice this concern earlier. Consequently, the property transaction with Blue Sun Capital LLC is deemed legally binding.
